name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,532

clue.text: Plunder picked up by boater? One intends to return things

indicators.note: In a down clue, lifting a word up reads it from the bottom

blocks.note: to plunder is to rob
someone out in a boat, pulling on the oars

explanation.surface: A thief's haul is scooped up by someone in a straw hat, while another person promises to hand everything back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boater' pretends to be the straw hat but is a person who rows; 'by' simply places the rower after the reversed plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrower takes things on loan with the understanding that they will be given back later, a playful dictionary-style paraphrase.

clue.text: Perform unaccompanied, soprano having left for dancing partner

indicators.note: Something that has left is gone

blocks.note: to gig is to play a live performance
alone, with no accompaniment
standard abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A singer is told to perform alone because the soprano has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface suggests a recital, and 'left' looks like a direction, but it only means the soprano's letter has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to escort and dance with women, so a hired dancing partner fits the traditional sense.

clue.text: Period in month that is not fully realised

indicators.note: Something not fully realised is incomplete, so the Latin phrase for 'that is' loses its final letter

blocks.note: the Latin id est, usually shortened to i.e.

explanation.surface: A part of the month that never quite came to fruition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' is the Latin ID EST; 'not fully realised' cuts its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the ides was a fixed day in the middle of each month, the 15th or 13th, so a dated period within it.

clue.text: Party dropping first court case

blocks.note: a faction is a party within a larger group

explanation.surface: A party gives up its first legal fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the F off FACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a lawsuit brought before a judge, so it is a formal proceeding heard in court.

clue.text: Never deviating, drink emptied daily, served with ice

indicators.note: Emptying a word removes its contents

blocks.note: a drink served on the rocks comes over ice
a common drink
just the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone never wavers: a daily drink downed, always on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emptied' applies to 'daily', not 'drink'; the ice phrase comes first in the answer though last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rock-steady is utterly firm and reliable, holding its course without wobbling or changing direction.

clue.text: Broadcast picked up in time: start of debate covering both opinions

indicators.note: In a down clue, picking up a word lifts it so it reads bottom to top
The start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, to sow
tide is an old word for time or season, as in Yuletide
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A broadcast debate, timed and opened fairly, gives airtime to both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' pretends to be radio; here it is the farming sense of scattering seed. Tide meaning time survives in words like Yuletide.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-sided discussion presents each of the opposing views, balanced between the rival positions.

clue.text: Scarecrow left on stick, attracting insect, with zero going around up top

indicators.note: Letters going around are spun into a new arrangement
In a down clue, up top is the head of the entry
In a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
Something that attracts draws another thing to it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for with
the word itself, to be jumbled
standard abbreviation for left
to gum something is to stick it
a tiny biting fly

explanation.surface: A scarecrow's parts: something on a stick drawing insects, with a round nought at the top for a head.
explanation.walkthrough: Worzel Gummidge is a talking scarecrow from British children's books and TV. 'Up top' puts W and jumbled ZERO at the head of the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Worzel Gummidge is the title character of Barbara Euphan Todd's stories, a turnip-headed field guardian who comes to life.

clue.text: I try latest in ontology, backing philosophy student

indicators.note: The latest letter of a word is its last
Backing means moving in reverse, so the whole string runs right to left

blocks.note: the pronoun as it stands
to have a go is to try
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A student of philosophy tries out the newest ideas in ontology.
explanation.walkthrough: Build I, GO, Y in clue order, then read the lot backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi is a disciple of yoga, a Hindu discipline of meditation and spiritual thought, hence a follower of that path.

clue.text: TV show repulsed nonsense and hoax - how peculiar

indicators.note: Something repulsed is driven back
A peculiar form is an odd one

blocks.note: rot is rubbish talk
cod is British slang for a spoof or hoax
the word itself, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A viewer recoils at a television programme full of rubbish and fakery, finding it rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: ROT and COD are joined and then reversed together; 'how' in 'how peculiar' is fodder, not an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction series about a time-travelling alien, a famous television programme.

clue.text: Something in Harry Potter - book having capacity to stay ahead of criticism

indicators.note: One piece staying ahead of another is placed before it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for book
room is space or capacity
to give someone stick is to criticise them, British slang

explanation.surface: A Harry Potter book is loaded enough to outrun its critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' tempts you towards a volume of the series, but it is just B. 'Stick' as criticism is British: 'the fans gave him stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wizards in the Potter novels fly on broomsticks, notably in the sport Quidditch, making it an item from those stories.

clue.text: Mass complaints in radio broadcast

indicators.note: A radio broadcast is heard rather than read

blocks.note: weary breaths of complaint

explanation.surface: A flood of listener complaints about a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a verb or a church service, but here it means bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass and size both describe how big or bulky something is, used loosely as synonyms.

clue.text: Weak device for transporting policeman finally engaged in one detective story

indicators.note: Being engaged in something is being occupied within it

blocks.note: w is a dictionary abbreviation for weak, as in the physics weak force
a hod is a trough for carrying bricks
a unit is a single thing
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A feeble plot about ferrying a policeman into a detective novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weak device' reads as one idea, but the adjective is just its abbreviation; a hod is a bricklayer's carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a crime novel or film built around the puzzle of identifying the murderer, a mystery tale.

clue.text: Not expected and possibly profound, eh?

indicators.note: Possibly signals one of several arrangements

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A surprise remark, perhaps a deep one, with a questioning 'eh?' tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'eh' is not filler: its two letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unhoped-for arrives without anyone having wished for or anticipated it, so it comes as a surprise.

clue.text: Was first to go round current shop

indicators.note: Going round means turning about

blocks.note: whoever led was out in front
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Being the first customer to walk around the local shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round' suggests surrounding something, but it only turns LED around; I then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a store selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Ocean feature getting cut, cut, cut? That’s to have added resonance

indicators.note: The third 'cut' trims the second one's synonym, taking off its last letter

blocks.note: a ridge of rock or coral near the surface
to chop is to cut

explanation.surface: Waves hit a reef over and over, the repeated word itself echoing in the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The three 'cut's do different jobs: the first trims REEF, the second means CHOP, the third trims that.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-echo is to reverberate again and again, a sound that rings on with extra repetition.

clue.text: Cross in middle of week over old car, producing curse

indicators.note: The middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters
In a down clue, one piece over another stands above it

blocks.note: the two central letters
a cross is shaped like X
a crate is slang for a battered old vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone crossed midweek by a clapped-out car, which makes them swear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like anger, fitting the swearing, but it is only the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down evil upon someone, the formal verb for cursing.

clue.text: Devoted attendant paid in the end, after rejection

indicators.note: Rejecting something throws it back

blocks.note: a goal is an end or aim
the standard abbreviation, as stamped on a bill

explanation.surface: A loyal servant finally gets paid, after being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: GOAL is reversed first to LAOG, then PD is slipped into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog, figuratively, is a fawning follower who serves someone slavishly, as a pampered pet stays close.

clue.text: See 7
Line out of fashion is a pain for the observer

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for line
style is fashion

explanation.surface: A dated look is painful for anyone who has to see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The observer' is someone's eye, where this pain sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed, sore swelling on the eyelid, so an ailment troubling someone who looks.

clue.text: Climbing expert brought in first boot accessory

indicators.note: In a down clue, a climbing word goes upward, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: an ace is a top performer
top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: A mountaineering guide is fetched in to supply premium boot gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing expert' reads as a mountaineer, but 'climbing' is the reversal signal for ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the reinforced covering over the front of a shoe or boot, fitted as protection.

clue.text: Insensitive sort? My dear chap, ignoring an American is dreadful

indicators.note: Ignoring a letter leaves it out
Something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the remaining letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of the phrase
A is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A tactless type is chided: 'My dear chap, ignoring an American is dreadful'.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two As goes, then the nine letters left are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A pachyderm is a thick-skinned animal such as an elephant, so figuratively a person impervious to criticism or feelings.

clue.text: Marsupial heading off after end of epic fight

indicators.note: The end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the final letter
a burrowing Australian marsupial

explanation.surface: A marsupial walks away after the climax of an epic brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed WOMBAT follows the C, even though the marsupial is named first.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is armed or physical conflict between opponents, a direct synonym for battle or struggle.

clue.text: Facilitate sound but not light, ultimately

indicators.note: Ultimately means in the end
'But not' excludes something

blocks.note: a sound argument is tenable, able to be defended
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Make it possible for sound, though not light, to travel in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is not noise here but the adjective, as in a sound argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to make something possible or easier, the same as to facilitate it.

clue.text: Many students are confused by term in algebra

indicators.note: Confused letters are muddled, so 'are' gets rearranged

blocks.note: y is a standard unknown in algebra
the word itself, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A class of pupils is baffled by a term in their algebra lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' pretends to be a school term; it is an algebraic term, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: In a school a year is the whole cohort of pupils of the same age, a large group of learners.

clue.text: About to include Republican in vernacular description of her opponents?

indicators.note: Including something takes it inside

blocks.note: demotic means of ordinary people's everyday speech
abbreviation of circa
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone describes the rivals of a Republican woman in plain everyday language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' refers back to the Republican: in US politics a Republican's opponents are Democrats, and the question mark flags that indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Democratic Party is the chief rival of the Republicans in US politics, so the adjective labels that side.

clue.text: Treat for dog, with dog getting energy for nothing

indicators.note: Getting one thing for another swaps them, so energy takes the place of nothing

blocks.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog; 'with' just attaches this second dog to the treat
the physics symbol for energy
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A dog's snack, the dog then finding energy from nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHOW the O becomes E.
explanation.definitionFit: A chew is a hard edible item, such as a rawhide, given to dogs to gnaw on.

clue.text: Navigational device - there - surrounded by a flashing light

blocks.note: a strobe is a light that flashes rapidly
la is an old exclamation meaning look there

explanation.surface: A ship's instrument, stuck out there amid a blinking beacon.
explanation.walkthrough: LA is an archaic interjection, like 'lo', calling attention to something.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe is an old instrument for measuring the altitude of stars, used by sailors to find their latitude.

clue.text: Undefined quantity in organisational symbol

blocks.note: a logarithm, a mathematical quantity
the argument zero, for which the function has no value

explanation.surface: An unspecified amount appears in a company emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The logarithm of zero is mathematically undefined, so 'undefined quantity' is LOG 0, read as LOG O.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is the emblem or badge a company or group uses to identify itself, its graphic mark.
